title: Expires must not appear more than once

spec.name: RFC 9116
spec.normative_quote: It is RECOMMENDED that the value of this field be less than a year into the future to avoid staleness. This field MUST always be present and MUST NOT appear more than once.
spec.note: Transcribed from a live fetch of https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9116.txt on 2026-08-31. The two sentences are adjacent in the source across a paragraph break, which normalizes to a single space; no words are altered and no passage is spliced. security-txt-expires-missing derives from the 'MUST always be present' half of the same sentence -- this rule derives from the 'MUST NOT appear more than once' half, which had no rule file and therefore could not be emitted at all.

policy_note: The gap this closes was structural, not a threshold choice: the validator matched Expires with a single non-global regex and silently used the FIRST match, so a second Expires line -- the exact case §2.5.5 forbids, and the case where a stale and a fresh date disagree -- was invisible. The validator now collects every Expires line and still evaluates the first for the expiry rules, so a duplicate file reports both the duplication and whatever the first value's expiry state is.
applicability: A security.txt body containing at least one Expires: field with a non-empty value.
expectation: Exactly one line matches /^Expires:[ \t]*\S/ (case-insensitive, per-line). Two or more is a violation regardless of whether the values agree.

cases.name: exactly one Expires field -- this rule does not fire
no Expires field -- this rule is inapplicable, security-txt-expires-missing fires instead
